keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the zones that the pages place in these years; the Tashkent countryside is gone from the shape on a confidence-1 bridge (no page dates its recovery).

ledger.note: 1918: the Basmachi rebellion 'started in earnest' after the February assault on Kokand, under Irgash Bey, 'Supreme Leader of the Islamic Army'; its roots lay in the anti-conscription violence of 1916. The place (Kokand) is the researcher's reading of where the rising began.

region.text: Ferghana and the countryside surrounding Tashkent

ledger.note: 1918: by the end of the year 'decentralized bands of fighters, totaling roughly 20,000, controlled Ferghana and the countryside surrounding Tashkent'. The page's snapshot is read as a gain from the Turkestan republic.

1920: the Tashkent countryside is lost to the Reds. No page dates this; bridged from Madamin Bey's defection 'to the Soviet side in March' (after the winter of 1919-20) and the Red Army's arrival in the republic in September 1919.

region.text: East Bukhara, 'roughly from Hisor to West Pamir' (BP); the Khatlon and Dushanbe admin-1s are a floor

ledger.note: 1921: the rebellion spreads to East Bukhara. 'Basmachi forces operated with success in both Khiva and Bokhara for an extended period' (1920-22); Enver Pasha 'joined the movement after November 1921'; he rejected a peace offer in May 1922, Kakurin's units beat the Basmachi at Kafrun in June, and on 4 August 1922 he was killed near Baldzhuan in a last cavalry charge. The region and year are the researcher's reading.
1924: Fergana is lost. A Ferghana presence under Korshirmat lasted 'until 1924'.

region.text: East Bukhara, 'roughly from Hisor to West Pamir' (BP); the Khatlon and Dushanbe admin-1s are a floor

ledger.note: 1925: Ibrahim Bek is beaten and East Bukhara lost. 'In the spring of 1925 Ibrahim Bek and his Basmachi were engaged and defeated by Red Army units of the Turkestan Military District'; from 1926 he raided from Kunduz and Aliabad in Afghanistan.

1934: the Basmachi movement ends. 'The Basmachi movement had ended by 1934'; the last major combat operation was in October 1933 and Ibrahim Bek, captured by Tajik villagers, was executed on 31 August 1931. No rebel-held land is dated after 1925.

sources.title: Basmachi movement
sources.note: Roots in 1916; the rebellion starts in earnest after the Kokand assault of February 1918; end of 1918 Fergana and the Tashkent countryside; Enver Pasha 1921-22; ended by 1934.

sources.title: Ibrahim Bek
sources.note: East Bukhara leader: defeated spring 1925, raids 1926-1931 from Kunduz and Aliabad, executed 31 August 1931.

sources.title: Bukharan People's Soviet Republic
sources.note: East Bukhara defined as roughly from Hisor to West Pamir; the Basmachi revolt sparked by the emir's overthrow.

notes: Written for batch ia-03-x from three pages (BM, IB, BP; budget 2-5). A movement more than a state: the pages give no capital, no area and no dated frontier, so every region is a reading and two events are confidence 1 (the loss of the Tashkent countryside; the spread to East Bukhara). The infobox span is 1916-1934; the dossier starts in 1918 because BM dates the rebellion 'in earnest' to after February 1918 and the 1916 revolt is Russian Turkestan's war. Not on the pages: Madamin Bey's Fergana zone dates, the Khiva front (Junaid Khan fled the Red Army in January 1920), the Kunduz and Aliabad bases in Afghanistan 1926-31 (not drawn as territory), Ibrahim Bek's districts. Counterparts bukharan-people-s-soviet-republic and turkestan-assr are written in this batch.
